result.judge_notes: pass 1 (A=with, B=without): A sets each breakpoint by when the content stops fitting, and shows the math that keeps the recipe column at 36rem or more. It also gives a complete CSS grid with explicit areas, deliberate handling of very wide screens and concrete tests for the developer. B has more width tiers, explicit 16px phone padding and useful UX extras. However, its breakpoints are standard device-named pixel values and its CSS is a thinner sketch that doesn't specify order or placement. | pass 2 (A=without, B=with): B ties each breakpoint to content fitting, shows the math (the recipe keeps at least 36rem, about 65ch) and uses em units. Its CSS is more complete and correct, with grid areas, a measure cap, reserved ad space and a container query. A covers more tiers and adds useful edge cases, but its breakpoints are labeled and chosen by device class, and its CSS sketch is thinner.
